visual_goal: Show Vantage as a service with a memory: every answer is appended to the ledger with fact and model versions, outcomes flow back to the same ledger, and model operations use it to back-test, watch bias by segment and trip circuit breakers.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration with a feedback loop on the right. Far left: a group of generic device icons (tablet, laptop, server) labeled 'Callers'. One arrow labeled 'request' into a central gateway box labeled 'Valuation API'. Above 'Valuation API', a box labeled 'Context assembler' with one arrow from the API up into it and one arrow back down labeled 'facts with versions'. Right of the API, a box labeled 'Model service' with one arrow from the API into it. One arrow from 'Model service' into a box with stacked plus and minus lines labeled 'Adjustment engine', and one arrow from 'Adjustment engine' back to 'Valuation API'. Below 'Valuation API', a large teal append-only ledger book labeled 'Valuation ledger', with one arrow from the API down into it labeled 'append first'. Lower left, a box with a handshake icon and a blank tag with no text, labeled 'Outcomes' with one arrow into the ledger labeled 'outcome links'. Lower right, a gear-and-chart box labeled 'Model operations' with one arrow pointing from the ledger rightward into 'Model operations' labeled 'bias by segment' (arrowhead at 'Model operations'), and one arrow from the top of 'Model operations' straight up ending with its arrowhead on the bottom edge of the 'Model service' box, labeled 'retrain'. Place 'Model operations' directly below 'Model service' so this arrow is vertical and crosses no other arrow.
alt: Callers ask the valuation API, which gathers versioned facts, scores with the model service and adjustment engine, and appends every answer to the valuation ledger; outcomes link back to the ledger, and model operations use it to measure bias by segment and retrain the model.

visual_goal: Show a trade-in valuation as swimlanes: the ledger write happens before the dealer sees the value, and the later offer links back to the same valuation id.
prompt: A left-to-right swimlane illustration with five vertical lanes, each headed by a simple icon and label: a tablet labeled 'Dealer app', a gateway labeled 'Valuation API', a folder-gathering box labeled 'Context assembler', a gear labeled 'Model service', and a ledger book labeled 'Valuation ledger'. Horizontal message arrows from top to bottom, in this order: from 'Dealer app' to 'Valuation API' labeled 'trade-in request'; from 'Valuation API' to 'Context assembler' labeled 'gather facts'; from 'Valuation API' to 'Model service' labeled 'score'; from 'Valuation API' to 'Valuation ledger' labeled 'append first', drawn in teal; from 'Valuation API' back to 'Dealer app' labeled 'typed answer'. Below a thin dashed divider, one orange arrow from 'Dealer app' to 'Valuation ledger' labeled 'offer, same id'.
alt: Swimlanes for dealer app, valuation API, context assembler, model service and valuation ledger: the API gathers facts, scores, appends to the ledger and then returns the typed answer; later the offer links to the ledger by the same valuation id.

visual_goal: Show segment drift monitoring: leading indicators from market data, dealer stock and trade channels plus ledger bias feed a segment monitor that widens ranges on watch and trips a per-segment circuit breaker on breach.
prompt: A top-to-bottom illustration. Top row: four small source boxes side by side, labeled 'Pulse', 'Lotwise', 'Tradefloor' and 'Valuation ledger', each with a tiny trend-line icon. Exactly four arrows down, one from each, into a central radar-screen box labeled 'Segment drift monitor'. From the monitor two arrows down: a left arrow labeled 'watch' into an amber box showing a widening bracket labeled 'Widen ranges', and a right arrow labeled 'breach' into a red box with a switch icon labeled 'Circuit breaker'. From 'Circuit breaker' two arrows down: one into a tablet box labeled 'Manual appraisal' and one into a gear box labeled 'Retrain'.
alt: Pulse, Lotwise, Tradefloor and the valuation ledger feed a segment drift monitor; on watch it widens ranges, on breach it trips a segment circuit breaker that switches appraisals to manual and triggers a retrain.
